sonnet.problem: The opening card says Saul set out with letters to Damascus's synagogues. Card 2 then asks where in Damascus Saul proclaims Jesus, and the answer is the synagogues. The setup gives the answer away.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

sonnet.problem: This True statement repeats what card 2 just asked and answered, that Saul proclaims Jesus in the synagogues. It also bundles the location and what he declares into one statement.
sonnet.rule: A True statement never just repeats the card before it. ... An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact.

sonnet.problem: The card tells a conspiracy to kill Saul (death and violence) and adds a joke: "He went from hunter to hunted... NOT a promotion anybody applies for."
sonnet.rule: A card that tells death, violence, abuse, serious sin or the body's private matters has no joke.

sonnet.problem: The card tells that they watch the gates to kill Saul and adds a joke: "Strolling out the front door of Damascus is off the table."
sonnet.rule: A card that tells death, violence, abuse, serious sin or the body's private matters has no joke.

sonnet.problem: This card re-asks the same fact as card 2. Both are about how the Jerusalem disciples view Saul in 9:26, afraid of him and not believing he is a disciple. The wrong answer "They welcome him right away" on card 2 already covers it.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question.

sonnet.problem: The card spends words defining "Grecian Jews" as "Jews who speak Greek." The passage text doesn't give that definition. It is an outside fact with no reference, and hard words get a dictionary pop-up instead.
sonnet.rule: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).
